\\---

  

  

  

\\\# 1. What PRV3 Is

  

  

  

PRV3 is a diagnostic instrument for organizational friction. An internal leader with budget authority — the Principal — takes the instrument. The engine identifies their organizational state. The output names the condition precisely and routes to a resolution recommendation. The diagnostic is the product. Everything else serves it.

  

  

  

The diagnostic is the primary entry point. Four resolution services sit beneath it: Groundwork, Development, First Call, Advisory. Service names locked Session 32. Two-tier structure locked Session 33. Pricing not locked.

  

  

  

\\---

  

  

  

\\\# 2. Governing Principles — Locked

  

  

  

| \\\*\\\*P-01\\\*\\\* | Questions that observe. Engine that infers. Output that names. |

  

| --- | --- |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-02\\\*\\\* | Clinical diagnostic that produces a felt experience. Framing-robust. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-03\\\*\\\* | Questions observe, users recognize. Scoring weight is invisible. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-04\\\*\\\* | Narrative prompt used surgically. Dynamically generated. Not static. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-05\\\*\\\* | Severity is an independent dimension. Three tiers: Emerging, Entrenched, Endemic. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-06\\\*\\\* | The instrument meets the user where they are. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-07\\\*\\\* | Two outputs, one session. Private (confrontational, felt). Shareable (professional, credible). |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-08\\\*\\\* | Design for maximum ambition, phase for practical execution. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-09\\\*\\\* | Economic visibility and behavioral diagnosis. Friction Tax + Behavioral Diagnosis. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-10\\\*\\\* | Brand voice: 40% blunt, 60% servant leader. Direct and warm. No coined terms. No passive constructions. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-11\\\*\\\* | Dual-axis dimensional scoring is locked. Four dimensions, two axes each. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-12\\\*\\\* | Scope discipline. Every addition answers: who does this serve and how? |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-13\\\*\\\* | Structural complexity needs a "how to read this" affordance before or alongside it, not after -- unexplained taxonomy reads as gimmick, not rigor. |

  

| \\\*\\\*P-14\\\*\\\* | When brand voice risks obscuring meaning, plain language wins -- don't make the reader do the work of decoding what could just be said directly. |

  

  

  

\\\*\\\*Additional governing constraint — confirmed Session 3\\\*\\\*

  

  

  

| \\\*\\\*Data-first calibration\\\*\\\* | Where a parameter cannot be derived from existing research or the taxonomy architecture, it is not set speculatively. The engine runs on neutral defaults. Calibration data drives differentiation. This applies to all numerical parameters in the scoring engine without exception. |

  

| --- | --- |

  

**Provisional Hold vs. Lock (Session 56):** Before a decision is recorded as Locked in the MOB, confirm whether any open async research threads could invalidate this constraint. If yes, the decision is a Provisional Hold until that thread closes. Provisional Holds are documented in the session log but not listed as Locked Decisions. When the thread closes, the hold converts to a Lock or the decision is revised. Example: displacement-pattern essay count was not locked during the research-refresh automation build because the de Waal verification thread was still open.

  

**P-13, source and first applications (confirmed 2026-08-16):** Pete's own framing this session: "It cannot be overstated how turned off our clients will be if they explore this AI-generated site and only see a gimmicky taxonomy without context. The taxonomy may be the least important detail." First two applications, both shipped before this principle was formally locked, retroactively named as the pattern's own precedent: the ConstellationField gestalt-interpretability addendum (Category E) and the /book/toc Gestalt Pass's Terminology Guide -- both independently built the same shape, a "what do these terms mean" affordance placed before or alongside the complex structural element itself, not after.

**P-14, source and first application (confirmed 2026-08-19):** Original candidate framing surfaced during the Category E Direction 1 Refinement session ("spoon-feed meaning when not speaking plainly in brand voice"), left NOT YET LOCKED at the time pending a comparison against P-13 (Session Priority Queue item 4). Refined and formally locked this session (Claude.ai): confirmed distinct from P-13, not a duplicate or superseded by it -- P-13 governs structural/visual complexity (taxonomies, diagrams) and is resolved with a "how to read this" affordance placed alongside the element; P-14 governs prose/word-choice clarity and is resolved by writing plainly in the first place, not by adding an explanatory layer next to brand-voice shorthand.

| --- | --- |

| \\\*\\\*Patterned Consequence Logic\\\*\\\* | Financial output section. Friction Tax computation. Not yet built. |

  

| \\\*\\\*JSON contract\\\*\\\* | 14 top-level fields. monitoring\\\_metadata added Session 11. ENGINE\\\_VERSION 0.2.0. |

\*\*Shareable output design intent — locked Session 34:\*\* The shareable output is designed to travel without the user present. It enters rooms the practitioner isn’t in — a board meeting, a budget conversation, a leadership team discussion about whether to engage outside help. Its job is to carry the condition’s financial weight and behavioral precision into those rooms and do the persuasion work required to justify the engagement before the practitioner arrives. Friction Tax multipliers (sourced from McKinsey, SHRM, Gallup, and peer-reviewed research) give the condition economic visibility. Patterned consequence logic gives it behavioral precision. The combination makes the condition undeniable to a financially-oriented audience. The shareable output never names a specific service. It names the condition, the severity, and the resolution family. Service recommendation is made by the practitioner in the live consultation — not by the instrument. This boundary is architecturally enforced, not aspirational.

\*\*Execution record:\*\*

- Gemini architectural review identified the core risk: the Python engine (resolution\_families.py) and the TypeScript web layer (web/lib/types.ts, both API route handlers) maintain independently hardcoded references to the four names with no shared contract. - Phase 1 (read-only scan, Claude Code): confirmed the legacy names function as both display strings and logic keys depending on file — RESOLUTION\_FALLBACK\_COPY's 26 tuple keys (19 single-service + 7 asymmetric compound) being the highest silent-failure risk, since a key mismatch degrades to generic fallback copy with no error or log.
- Phase 2, Step 1 (Python core + test suite): ENGINE\_TO\_COMMERCIAL\_NAME values updated; all 26 RESOLUTION\_FALLBACK\_COPY keys and associated body copy renamed; tools/test\_resolution\_families.py assertions updated in the same pass. engine/data/states.py explicitly excluded — its "Development" value is pre-translation, engine-internal taxonomy vocabulary, a different semantic layer from the commercial name, and was confirmed to carry zero diff throughout. Checkpoint A: 101/101 tests passing.

Checkpoint B: tsc --noEmit, 0 errors. Post-write identicality between both route handlers confirmed.

\*\*Self-selection interface — Architecture Spec v0.2 — locked Session 35:\*\* Four-phase architecture confirmed and build-ready. \\\*\\\*Asset field standard — correction, Session 29:\\\*\\\* State-vector asset fields are NOT at 0.4000. The prior "all 7 other fields = 0.15" phrasing in the tier descriptions referred to the off-axis liability fields plus assets being at tier-standard values — it was NOT an 8-field sum. Any vector reshape must preserve the 0.90 liability budget and leave asset fields at tier standard unless Phase 3 asset calibration is explicitly authorized.

| INDUSTRY_NON_EXEMPT_RATIO citation-accuracy gap — documentation-reliability finding, inverse case | Addendum 10 (prompts/friction-tax-legal-compliance-methodology.md) presented INDUSTRY_NON_EXEMPT_RATIO as "real BLS data," explicitly contrasted against two OTHER things in the same addendum it labeled as undocumented judgment calls -- the confident, sourced-looking one turned out to be the one with the real problem. | Weak-branch weighted-damping redesign -- WEAK_UNWIRED_DAMPING_FACTOR chosen on design intent, not measured discrimination | Session 70's damped weak-branch routing applied the same dimension-level damped signal to every question in a weak-tier profile, wired or not -- confirmed this session to mean any two states sharing a primary_dimension get byte-for-byte identical weak-branch answer vectors, a real same-dimension-blindness gap. A first fix attempt (hard-gate: real signal only for state_targets-wired questions, pure _neutral_option() noise otherwise) caused a genuine regression -- 6 states moved from passing to failing at the weak tier (cultural_overtime, human_displacement_anxiety, leadership_deafness, motivational_architecture_failure, sequential_decision_blindness, the_untouchable), zero new passes anywhere, confirmed via full before/after diff. Reverted, not committed. **Redesign (this finding, committed):** wired questions now use best_option_for_state() -- real, full-strength signal, same function moderate/high_confidence already use -- while unwired questions keep _damped_weak_option()'s dimension-level signal at a further down-weighted threshold (WEAK_DAMPED_THRESHOLD * WEAK_UNWIRED_DAMPING_FACTOR) rather than being zeroed. Full 172-profile suite recovers to 169/172, byte-for-byte identical by-state breakdown to the pre-redesign baseline (confirmed via diff, not just matching totals); moderate/high_confidence entirely unaffected (54/57, same 3 pre-existing failures, unmoved). **The honest caveat, logged so it doesn't get lost in a commit message:** WEAK_UNWIRED_DAMPING_FACTOR = 0.4 was NOT arrived at because the test suite showed it outperforming other values -- every value tested from 0.0 to 1.0 (0.0, 0.02, 0.05, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0) produced a byte-for-byte identical by-state result, including 0.0, which is mathematically equivalent to the failed hard-gate's unwired behavior (0 < contribution <= 0 is never true, so it always falls through to _neutral_option()). The real regression-fixing change is routing wired questions through best_option_for_state()'s unbounded signal instead of keeping them on the old damped, bounded-at-0.25 function -- that alone recovers the baseline regardless of the unwired damping value. 0.4 was chosen to honor the qualitative design intent (unwired questions should carry some real, non-zero, meaningfully-damped signal, not be reduced to pure noise) even though nothing in the current 172-profile suite can confirm that choice matters over any other value in range. This is genuinely untested territory pending future calibration profiles that exercise thinly-wired, same-dimension state pairs directly -- worth revisiting if such profiles are ever added, not a precisely-tuned number today. |

| Legal/Compliance channel -- actuarial tail-risk distinction | 3 | Open -- flagged, not scoped, queued behind the multi-state compounding redesign | Raised during an actuarial-framing review of the Friction Tax scoring methodology. Turnover, Productivity, and Decision-Quality behave as attritional risk -- steady, expected, frequency-driven costs, well-suited to proportional blending on a shared 0-2 scale. Legal/Compliance behaves more like a tail/catastrophic peril -- rare, but severe when realized -- and is not well-modeled by the same proportional blending used for the other three channels. Standard actuarial practice prices these two risk types with different methods (expected-value pricing for attritional, separate large-loss loading for tail risk) rather than folding both into one blended severity score. Current Set 3 rubric scores Legal on the same 0-2 scale as the other three and sums it into the same raw total -- this may understate the "beyond question" credibility bar for that specific channel. Sequencing: explicitly queued behind the multi-state compounding mechanism (state-count/Factor A/Factor B) -- do not start design work on this until that item is resolved and reopened by Pete | This session (Claude Code) | Pete's call -- reopen after multi-state compounding design is finalized |

| **Quarterly Step-Back redefined: dual-sourced, source-verified process, not a single-question resolution session** | Governing-principle-level change to how the standing Quarterly Step-Back cadence (CLAUDE.md, roughly every 3 weeks) actually runs, effective this session. Supersedes the informal single-question-resolution precedent (the 2026-08-22 visual-identity-philosophy step-back, itself real and valuable but not run to this template). **New required process:** (1) Claude.ai produces an initial project evaluation -- status, business viability, SWOT, recommendations -- using whatever context it has (memory, conversation search, project knowledge). (2) Claude Code independently re-verifies it cold, from direct source only (code, content, commit history, live MOB), without reading Claude.ai's version first, producing its own full five-part assessment (ground-truth audit, viability assessment, SWOT, forward recommendations, comparison note) so it cannot be anchored by Claude.ai's framing. (3) Discrepancies are resolved against live source, not by deferring to whichever assessment sounds more confident -- every claim that doesn't survive CC's direct verification is corrected, with the root cause of the error named where useful (a stale MOB entry, a misleading code comment, a claim never actually verified). (4) The resulting reconciled, verified picture -- not either assessment alone -- is what drives the next work plan. **Why this exists, stated plainly:** this session's Round 1 (Claude.ai, conversation-history-based) assessment gave Pete at least two materially wrong claims -- that the friction-tax pricing engine wasn't built, and that resolution-family copy was still "COPY PENDING" -- both traced to stale historical summaries rather than current source. Round 2 (Claude Code, cold, source-verified) confirmed both errors, named their root causes (a stale July MOB entry claiming STATE_MULTIPLIERS was unpopulated, true when written but stale by the time it was cited; literal leftover "COPY PENDING" comments sitting over genuinely finished, Pete-approved authored prose), and surfaced a new finding neither prior pass caught -- this file's own Decision Register contained two directly contradicting rows on whether Path 1 (the full diagnostic instrument) was built. This project already applies independent-verification discipline to Gemini's claims and to CC's own self-verification; this decision extends that same discipline to Claude.ai's strategic assessments specifically, since those are what drive real business decisions and are exactly where the discipline was missing before this run. **First run and standing artifacts:** `prompts/prv3-comprehensive-assessment-cc.md` -- the authoritative, source-verified five-part assessment from this run -- and `prompts/prv3-quarterly-step-back-2026-08-23.md` -- the process-definition document itself, recording both the new required format and this run's own trace. Both committed to the repo as the durable reference for how every future Quarterly Step-Back should be run. **Reconciliation note, added same session:** this row's own two named examples (friction-tax status, resolution-family copy status) describe errors already corrected before this row was written -- they need no further action.
